withdrawal_reasons: harness/control-plane state observation only — not an economic receipt and not an engine-TTFT receipt
no buyer charges, supplier payables, ledger conservation, or physical-work counters are recorded
does not measure TTFT, throughput, or GPU reuse against a live engine under controlled conditions
must not be cited as a production work-elimination or performance receipt
method: three batch jobs sharing a long leading system prompt with different tails, submitted to a running control plane served by a real Apple Silicon worker
meaning: Three independent jobs converged on the same prefix ids at three depths, so the scheduler can route a later job to whichever supplier already holds that KV cache instead of paying prefill again. A centralized host does this inside its own fleet; this does it across independent suppliers.
ordering_verified: cheaper_class_online ASC and cheaper_ask_online ASC sort ABOVE warm_prefix_depth DESC in the claim ORDER BY, so a warm expensive worker never displaces a cold cheap one. Warmth is order-only and never a WHERE predicate, so a cold job is never starved.
not_demonstrated_live: Preference BETWEEN workers needs two workers of the same cost class; only one worker was connected. Grok's wiring tests cover that case, and this run proves the state those tests depend on is actually produced by real traffic.
not_wired: batch_policy.go remains unwired. Workers claim one task per poll and intra-task batching lives in the Rust agent, so there is no control-plane call site. Reported rather than fake-wired.
note: WITHDRAWN. Retained as historical harness observation only. Do not cite as a live economic or engine performance proof. Controlled prefix-affinity routing measurement (stand-in) lives under evidence/perf/prefix-affinity-routing.json when sealed with MERC_PREFIX_AFFINITY_PERF=1.
